extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Browse's Collections list now opens straight away. On a large library it had to prepare every single collection before it could show you the first one, which meant a wait of several seconds each time you opened the section -- and much longer the first time. It now prepares only what is on screen, and the rest as you scroll to it. - If you change Kodi skin, tofa now offers to add its fonts to the new skin. Previously, saying no to that once meant you were never asked again, even on a different skin where the fonts really were missing, and tofa's own screens were left using whatever the skin happened to supply.

extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - Picture subtitles stored inside a film's own file (VobSub) now appear in the subtitle list when the file plays directly. They used to be offered only burnt into the picture, which meant re-encoding the whole video for a subtitle track. Needs tofa server 0.9.33, which is now the version this add-on is built against. - Collections people make on your server now show up in Browse, ahead of the catalogue's own franchise sets. Open one to see what's in it; making and editing them stays in tofa's web app for now. Needs tofa server 0.9.33. - "Always show subtitles" no longer gives up when no track matches your preferred language: it now tries the language of the audio you are hearing, then a track with no language label, before leaving subtitles off. The same order tofa's web player uses. - A converted stream that cannot start straight away -- usually because a just-stopped stream is still letting go of the server's graphics card -- now gets a second chance two seconds later instead of an error message.

An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - When a title will not load because your server is busy rather than unreachable, tofa now says so. It used to tell you to check your connection even when the connection was fine and the server was simply taking too long to answer, which sent you looking at the one part that was working. - Cast & Crew fills in one go. The photographs used to arrive a few at a time, leaving half the panel empty for several seconds on a 4K box; tofa now collects them while you are still on the title's main page. The People results in Search are quicker for the same reason. - Discover and Collections fill the same way. Their artwork comes from tofa's cloud rather than from your own server, and Kodi was filing every picture away itself before it drew it -- on a cold Discover tab that took twenty seconds. tofa now fetches what is on screen up front and the rest quietly behind it. - tofa no longer leaves background work and open connections behind when it has finished with a screen. On a box left running all day this showed up as memory creeping upwards. - Continue Watching only says how much is left when there is something left. Once you finish an episode the next one takes its place on that row, and tofa was labelling it with the whole episode's running time as though you were already part-way through -- while drawing no progress bar under it, which is what gave it away.

extension.summary: Install and update the tofa add-on
extension.description: The update channel for tofa's Kodi add-on. Installing this repository lets Kodi fetch the add-on and every later release on its own.
